title: Anyone using one Codex session to coordinate game, website and QA work?
author: Big-Passenger-4723
selftext:
I've been trying this in the Codex App while working across a game, its website and QA. Curious how other people here are handling it.

I keep one main session for discussing requirements and plans, then ask it to send specific tasks to the existing sessions responsible for those projects. It collects results, checks the work and sends issues back for another pass. I still open the execution sessions myself to look at their approach and adjust things when needed.

A recent example was a website prototype: I discussed the requirements in the main session, had it hand the task to Website Builder, then check the returned mock and request revisions. I wanted something clickable to review before implementation.

A typical instruction would be:

"Find the Website Builder session and confirm it's the right one. Send it the requirements we just agreed on. Ask for a clickable mock first, review the result, and send back anything that needs fixing. Wait for my review before implementation."

My starting point was keeping each session focused on its project's context. In practice, I also spend less time copying messages between them. The handoffs still need the relevant requirements and decisions.

The part I'm still thinking through is shared files. These sessions can use the same working directory, so they can still overwrite each other's changes. I haven't used Git worktrees for this setup yet. Separate directories would help with that, but integration still needs an owner.

For those doing this on game projects: do you give each session a separate worktree, or keep one checkout with clear file ownership? Who handles shared changes and checks that the pieces work together?

replies.body: "Codex" isn't a model. I've had Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT $200 plans and they're all comparable. You actually need all three since each one does something best that the other can't. It's all coordinated
